1160	And it came to pass one day that, even so, one of
1161	the sons who brought Dad tefillin
1162	found out at the last moment that they were Rabbeinu Tam's, and took them off after Dad's question.
1163	And indeed Dad caught it at the last moment, before reciting the blessing, and they switched him to Rashi's before Rabbeinu Tam's.
1164	But there was a somewhat more inward case, that happened once
1165	when the son had already gotten used to this question and answered automatically, "Yes, yes, it's Rashi," "Yes, yes, it's Rabbeinu Tam."
1166	A mistake came out, and Dad recited the blessing on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1167	And afterward: "Oy, what have I done?"
1168	The son came and apologized.
1169	Then came the consolations. It is written in the holy books that every person will happen
1170	once in his life to err and recite the blessing on Rabbeinu Tam's.
1171	Before Rashi's, it will happen to him once in his life. So it is brought in the book Taamei HaMinhagim, which says:
1172	a tradition from holy men that the man who is careful all his days to put on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin and never lacks them
1173	all his days through any mishap, will surely be made to recite the blessing once on Rashi's tefillin
1174	the blessings, and pray in them.
1175	He also cites there the book Yakar Totafta, written by a kabbalist in the name of Rav Mordechai of Dubrovna,
1176	that Rabbeinu Tam acted in the heavenly court that whoever puts on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin will be made, at the very least, once
1177	in his life to err and put on, with a blessing, Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin instead of Rashi's.
1178	And that there is such a tradition in the name of the holy Rav of Lublin, and afterward he brings more books there, and so on.
1179	In any case, for our purposes, even the mistake that happened with my father
1180	was by deliberate Providence from Heaven, for so it had to be, because Rabbeinu Tam asked in Heaven that whoever it may be,
1181	once he will come to a mistake,
1182	so that he will get to bless and pray with Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1183	But our father was a meticulous man, very meticulous, between man and his fellow, between man
1184	and the Place, especially in monetary matters.
1185	For several years he would receive in the mail a calendar, the
1186	Or HaChaim calendar of the Or HaChaim yeshivah in Jerusalem; they would send it to him by mail every year.
1187	Right away our father would sit down, that very day he would sit and send them back
1188	an envelope with payment. Once we asked him:
1189	Why do they send it to you, and why do you pay what you never even asked for, and we already have a calendar
1190	at home? He answered that apparently once I donated to them
1191	and since then they send it to me regularly. Since they take the trouble to send it and also enclose a return
1192	payment envelope, they expect to receive, so I don't change from what I did
1193	at the beginning, the first time. And so he kept paying for the calendar even though he owed them nothing; he hadn't asked
1194	that they send it again, but if they already send it and have grown used to it, then I keep on too
1195	with what I did the first time. Caution in monetary matters, caution
1196	in his own monetary matters, on account of another's, yes?
1197	One who is careful in monetary matters is called a tzaddik. "A righteous man," Noach, "ish tzaddik."
1198	Our Sages tell us, the Gemara says: a tzaddik in money.
1199	As we produced a comprehensive shiur on the subject, called "Ish Tzaddik."
